summary: run_init now stops harness-<run>-svc, then runs INIT_CMD in it (MemoryMax=SVC_MEMORY_MAX 3G, timeout -k 10s INIT_TIMEOUT 10m, stdin /dev/null); a refused unit notes `init ran uncapped`. Stub systemd-run refuses a still-loaded unit like real systemd. 4 checks (3 seen RED), decision file, arch/README/config docs. Tests 270 → 274.
verified_how: RED on a git copy with the old driver: the dup-unit, the stop-then-scope order and the backgrounded-init checks failed (bare check passed, as a regression guard). GREEN: lib/check.sh green in 473 s, 274/274; no harness-test-* unit or sleep 300 left. Opus review: 0 Critical/Important, 3 Minor (2 fixed).

dead_ends.tried: running the RED suite on a tar copy of the tree without git
dead_ends.why: the eval checks need a git repo; git init + commit in the copy works

discoveries.text: stub-systemd-run.sh now refuses a unit whose .alive is set and that is .running or holds a live pid (fixtures/systemd-run-unit-exists.txt, exit 1, command not run). Any new code that reuses a unit name must scope_stop it first.

run_init sets SVC_UP=1 before the start (plan §1); services_down (L2-03) can key on it. The bp1 check (tests/run.sh ~960) counts `stop harness-bp1-svc.scope` >= 2, so finish's stop in L2-03 keeps it green.

GNU timeout (no --foreground) kills its whole process group on expiry, so an init that times out takes the servers it already backgrounded with it; docs say so. Plan's `timeout -k 10s 10m` kept as the step names it.

Review Minor not fixed: run ids are unique per project only, and scope_unit maps . to -, so two projects' runs with the same id share harness-<id>-svc and run_init's stop-first would kill the other's services (was: refused, bare). gc's unit match (L2-05) has the same ambiguity; consider the project in the unit name or refusing a duplicate id.

questions: D *default* (decisions/2026-10-25-services-scope): the init's stdin is now /dev/null instead of the tmux pane, so an interactive init prompt fails fast instead of waiting for you in the window. OK?
